title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the neighbouring pages): Grothendieck works with a profinite group 𝔖 (written 𝔊 in the transcription). It is a quotient of the profinite completion 𝔖_{0,3}^{+∧} of the modular group PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3, with generators σ (σ²=1) and ρ (ρ³=1). He attaches to (𝔖,ρ,σ) the following objects.
- G_{ρ,σ}: a group of automorphisms of 𝔖 compatible with the data (ρ,σ).
- B_{ρ,σ} = Σ_{ρ,σ}: a 'Borel-like' group of pairs (ξ,η), solutions of the 'équation des lacets'.
- L_0 ≅ Ẑ: the cyclic group of inner automorphisms by the loop ε (powers of the 'unipotent' loop). These encode the ambiguity of a tangential base point.
- Γ_{ρ,σ} = B_{ρ,σ}/L_0 ≅ G_{ρ,σ}/𝔖. These are the exact sequences (20 bis): 1→L_0→B→Γ→1 and 1→𝔖→G→Γ→1.
On the previous page, for 𝔖 = SL(2,Ẑ)' one finds Γ ≅ Ĝ_m = Ẑ^*, B = B'_0 (Borel of the level-0 modular structure) and G = GL(2,Ẑ)'. So the procedure recovers the cyclotomic/linear 'arithmetic' group from the geometric group.

This page:
(i) In the general case one should not expect Γ_{ρ,σ} to be small, e.g. commutative. In the 'universal' case 𝔖 = 𝔖_{0,3}^{+∧}:
- (23) B_{ρ,σ} = M̃_{0,3}[0]' = Ker(ε_3: M̃_{0,3}[0]→{±1}).
- (24) Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Π̃'_{0,3} ⊃ Π'_ℚ. That is, Γ is (an index-2 piece of) the automorphism group of the genus-0 Teichmüller tower in the Longue Marche notation. It contains (the corresponding subgroup of) Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ). This is the GT-hat-type group, containing Galois via Belyi.
(ii) Under suitable conditions the extension 1→L_0→B→Γ→1 should split. Assume σ²=ρ³=1, so 𝔖 is a quotient of 𝔖_{0,3}^{+∧}. Assume also that 𝔖 is 'large enough' to map onto the linear quotient PL(Ẑ) (PSL/PGL(2,Ẑ)). Then:
- B ≃ Σ_{ρ,σ} maps to the Borel B̃'_{0,3}.
- T_{ρ,σ} is defined as the inverse image of the torus T̃_0.
- B'_0 = T_0 ⋉ (image of L_0) with L_0 mapping isomorphically to the unipotent radical. So T ∩ L_0 = 1 and B = T·L_0.
- Hence T_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} is an isomorphism (25). T is then a section both of B→Γ and of G→Γ.
- (26): B ≅ T ⋉ L_0 and G ≅ T ⋉ 𝔖 (semidirect).
In GT language, this is the normalization of an element (λ,f) by requiring its 'linear/abelian' image to be diagonal (f in the commutator subgroup). It kills the ambiguity of conjugation by powers of the loop at the tangential base point. The next page then sets up the solution set 𝒢_{ρ,σ} of the loop equations α ρ(α)^{-1} = β σ(β)^{-1} ε_1^ν.
errors: Notation drift: the quotient is written γ_{ρ,σ} on this page but Γ_{ρ,σ} on the previous page. They are evidently the same group.

The splitting argument tacitly needs L_0 to map injectively onto the unipotent part of B̃'_{0,3} (true when L_0 ≅ Ẑ maps to the profinite unipotent ≅ Ẑ). It also needs B's image to lie in T_0·U. Neither is stated, but both are plausible under the 'assez grand' hypothesis.

(24) is asserted ('on aura') without proof. It depends on identifying B in the universal case with the Teichmüller-tower automorphism group M̃_{0,3}[0]', which is a substantive claim analogous to the definition of GT-hat.

ideas.what: For any profinite quotient 𝔖 of PSL(2,Ẑ) with marked ρ, σ: define B, G, Γ by loop equations. Γ recovers Ẑ^* for 𝔖 = SL2(Ẑ)', and a group containing Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ) for the universal case.
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT-hat and its finite/quotient analogues ('GT-shadows')
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990), Ihara (1990s) for GT-hat; Dolgushev et al. (2020s) for GT-shadows of finite quotients
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981) sketch the Teichmüller-tower group containing Galois. This quotient-by-quotient formalism is only in these manuscripts.

ideas.what: Γ_{ρ,σ} ⊃ Gal(ℚ̄/ℚ)' in the universal case
Splitting B = T ⋉ L_0 and G = T ⋉ 𝔖 via the inverse image of the torus under the map to the linear quotient
ideas.modern_name: Normalization of GT elements / tangential base point (f in the commutator subgroup)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld; Ihara (standard normalization in GT theory)

missed.claim: The page frames a 'GT-type' group Γ_{ρ,σ} attached to each quotient 𝔖 of PSL(2,Ẑ). It interpolates between Ẑ^* (linear quotient, giving GL2) and the GT/Teichmüller group (universal quotient). It also gives a splitting criterion: 𝔖 must dominate PSL(2,Ẑ). This is close in spirit to the recent theory of GT-shadows for finite-index quotients, and to the study of 'Galois-type images' of quotients of π_1(M_{1,1}). Those works do not cite this formalism.
missed.quote: il ne faut pas ... s'attendre : à ce que γ_{ρ,σ} soit aussi petit — p.ex. qu'il soit commutatif ... (24) γ_{ρ,σ} ≃ Π̃'_{0,3} (⊃ Π'_ℚ !)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historical precursor to the GT-shadow programme (Dolgushev and coauthors). The idea of computing Γ for intermediate quotients, e.g. congruence or noncongruence quotients, could be compared with known results on GT-shadows.

deep.surprise_reason: The page anticipates GT-hat-like structures for arbitrary quotients and gives a clean splitting criterion. However, the GT/Galois inclusion is known to be in the Esquisse, and the splitting is the standard normalization. The quotient-by-quotient viewpoint is a mildly notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: 'il ne faut pas dans H s'attendre' is likely 'il ne faut pas du tout s'attendre'.
'on doit pouvoir dans [?] circonstances convenables' is likely 'dans certaines circonstances convenables'.
γ_{ρ,σ} should be read as Γ_{ρ,σ}, consistent with (19)–(21) on the previous page.
'on nécessairement [?] suppose' is likely 'on suppose nécessairement' or 'on a nécessairement'.
'⊂ PL(Ẑ) [?])' probably refers to the linear quotient PSL/PGL(2,Ẑ), the 'GP(Ẑ)' notation of the previous page.
In (24) the target is Π̃'_{0,3} (the Teichmüller-tower group of Longue Marche) and the parenthesis reads '(⊃ Π'_ℚ !)'.
